resolvedReview.overview:
This PR changes `Cache.get` to return freshness metadata: the signature goes from `Promise<string | null>` to `Promise<{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null>`, backed by `this.store.readWithMetadata(key)` instead of `this.store.read(key)`. `src/profile.ts` re-touches its cache-hit line without adapting it.

Despite the PR description ("preserving existing contracts"), the return contract of `get()` did change, and its only caller, `loadProfile()`, still consumes the result as a string. That mismatch breaks every non-null cache hit, so the patch cannot merge as-is.

findings.title: [P1] Update `loadProfile` to parse `cached.value` after the cache return-type change
findings.body: `src/cache.ts:5-6` changes `get()` to return `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null`, but the caller in `src/profile.ts:19` still executes `JSON.parse(cached)` on the whole object. `JSON.parse` requires a string: in a transpile-only build, every non-null profile cache hit coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws a `SyntaxError`; under `tsc` type-checking it is a compile error. Fix the caller, e.g. `return JSON.parse(cached.value);`, and decide whether `cached.stale` should influence the hit (the flag is currently read by no one).

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR changes `Cache.get` to return freshness metadata: the signature goes from `Promise<string | null>` to `Promise<{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null>`, backed by `this.store.readWithMetadata(key)` instead of `this.store.read(key)`. `src/profile.ts` re-touches its cache-hit line without adapting it.

Despite the PR description ("preserving existing contracts"), the return contract of `get()` did change, and its only caller, `loadProfile()`, still consumes the result as a string. That mismatch breaks every non-null cache hit, so the patch cannot merge as-is.

## Verification

## Findings

### [P1] Update `loadProfile` to parse `cached.value` after the cache return-type change
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** `src/cache.ts:5-6` changes `get()` to return `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null`, but the caller in `src/profile.ts:19` still executes `JSON.parse(cached)` on the whole object. `JSON.parse` requires a string: in a transpile-only build, every non-null profile cache hit coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws a `SyntaxError`; under `tsc` type-checking it is a compile error. Fix the caller, e.g. `return JSON.parse(cached.value);`, and decide whether `cached.stale` should influence the hit (the flag is currently read by no one).
**Location:** `src/profile.ts:19 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

The `correctness` and `performance-resources` lanes first returned `partial`; both preserved raw "NO FINDINGS" evidence. `correctness` completed cleanly on rerun (NO FINDINGS). `performance-resources` was partial again on rerun with the same raw output, so I covered that lens inline: the diff introduces no loops, allocations, I/O changes, or resource-ownership changes — no findings. All other lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes

- Exposing cache freshness metadata is a reasonable capability, and the async shape and nullability contract are preserved.
- Correctness: the P1 above is the only defect; the fix is a one-line caller update (plus a `stale` policy decision).
- Security: no security regressions in the changed lines; the `JSON.parse` trust surface is unchanged once the caller reads `cached.value`.
- Performance: no performance or resource concerns introduced.
